A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RRPO research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including the additional Appendix J in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original RRPO experiments on HotpotQA, AmbigNQ, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and MuSiQue, together with ablations and generalization analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and analyses. The separately attributed DynamicRAG result in its new comparison does not alter this assessment.

M1.justification: The sequential selection policy, PPO-style objective, reference-anchored baseline, advantage normalization, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Appendix J describes the existing modular approach without introducing a new component or procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four QA datasets and retain the same reader, prompt, and retrieval scenarios. Appendix J compares methods on the already-covered HotpotQA dataset.

E2.justification: Table 12 adds DynamicRAG (LLaMA-2) as a reported comparator using an explicitly cited result. V1 discusses DynamicRAG only in related work. Existing comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The retained splits, retrieval pool, document counts, readers, metrics, and training settings are unchanged. Appendix J juxtaposes existing RRPO scores with a cited DynamicRAG score; it does not document a new matched evaluation protocol or revised experiment settings.

E4.justification: The interaction-depth ablation, reader transfer, prompt robustness, smaller-supervisor experiments, and alternative RL architecture analyses are retained. Appendix J adds a baseline comparison, without a new ablation, robustness test, or error analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix H and Table 11 retain the same means, standard deviations, paired per-query F1 t-tests, and p < 0.01 statements. No run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 12 adds DynamicRAG's cited 29.40 EM alongside existing RRPO scores of 28.12, 29.26, and 30.03 for bge, jina, and gte. Table 9 changes the Qwen2.5-7B + GTE F1 from 41.23 to 31.94, contradicting the unchanged 41.23 in Tables 1 and 6. Other retained results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the same MDP definitions, policy equations, objective, advantage calculation, and baseline formulation. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, propositions, or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The introduction qualifies its categorical statement that standard approaches 'fail to optimize' generation quality to 'may not explicitly optimize' it. The abstract and conclusion retain the same RRPO contributions and headline performance, transfer, and robustness claims.

C2.justification: Appendix J adds an efficiency interpretation contrasting lightweight reranker optimization with DynamicRAG's joint training, while explicitly acknowledging an asymmetric comparison. Existing mechanism explanations and the limitation concerning initial retrieval recall remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a first-page public code repository link and explicitly reports approximately 0.3B parameters for the encoder rerankers in Appendix J. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, prompts, and acceleration details in the appendices are unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix J expands positioning against the already-cited DynamicRAG, emphasizing modular reranker training with a frozen reader versus joint LLM training. Bibliographic updates otherwise identify the same works and primarily supply publication metadata.

P1.justification: V2 makes limited introduction and related-work wording edits, revises author affiliations and contribution notes, adds acknowledgements, updates bibliographic metadata, and appends Section J. The existing narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 12 with method, model-size, and EM columns. Figure 2 moves from PDF page 6 to page 7, several tables shift position, and the first-page header and footnotes change. Existing figures and table structures are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: The code link and expanded research positioning provide useful additions. However, Appendix J relies on an explicitly asymmetric, cross-paper comparison, and Table 9 introduces an unexplained F1 inconsistency: 31.94 replaces 41.23 while Tables 1 and 6 retain 41.23. With the core scientific evidence unchanged, these limited benefits and reporting harms do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
